instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of rice in a pot until the water runs mostly clear. Add 1 3/4 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered.
While the rice cooks, wrap the tofu blocks in a clean kitchen towel. Set a heavy pan on top and press for 10 minutes.
Peel the apple and grate it on the large holes of a box grater into a medium bowl. Grate 2 teaspoons of ginger into the same bowl. That should be about 2/3 cup of apple.
Mince the garlic and add it to the bowl with 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp gochujang, 3 tbsp sesame oil and 3 tbsp sugar. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Slice the green onions, white and green parts together, and set them aside.
Slice the cucumbers thin and transfer them to a small bowl. Toss with 1 tbsp of the sesame seeds and a pinch of the salt.
Unwrap the tofu and grate it on the large holes of the box grater into a bowl. Sprinkle 1/4 tsp salt over the top and toss gently.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add half the oil, then half the grated tofu in an even layer. Leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the bottom is golden. Stir and cook for 3 minutes, until the edges are crisp. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil to the skillet and cook the remaining tofu the same way.

Turn the heat to medium and return all the tofu to the skillet. Pour in the sauce and stir. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and clings to the tofu with no liquid left in the pan.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in most of the green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Spoon the rice into bowls and put the tofu on top. Add the cucumbers on the side and finish with the remaining green onions and sesame seeds. Set the gochujang on the table for anyone who wants more heat.
method_notes: The lead is a grated, crisped tofu that takes a sweet apple-gochujang sauce, which the other versions mostly agree on (soy, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, a grated apple or pear). Others slice the tofu and marinate it, or coat cubes in cornstarch; those need a 30 minute to 2 hour marinade, so this follows the lead and pan-fries instead of air frying. Gochujang is cut to 1 tbsp so the base stays mild, with more at the table. The lead's rating is the page's visible 4.91 from 76 votes. The sliced-tofu pages had a single vote or none, and the cornstarch one had no ratings.
